subject: Procurement routing: marketplace billing vs direct MSA — support & escalation model
messages:
From: Katie Lin <procurement@nimbusanalytics.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
Cc: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-04-19T08:14:00-07:00
Subject: Procurement routing: marketplace billing vs direct MSA — support & escalation model

Hi Jordan,

Following up on our procurement checklist: our legal and IT teams want to understand the implications of buying Redwood via AWS/Azure/GCP marketplace listing versus signing a direct MSA with Redwood (or a co-sell path). Two specific concerns have come up:

1) Support ownership and escalation — if we buy via marketplace, who owns Tier 1/Tier 2 ticket routing? Do we still escalate to Redwood engineers or is that mediated through the cloud vendor?
2) Invoice/PO flow and revenue recognition — we need to know whether the invoice will come from Redwood or the marketplace reseller and whether that affects our vendor onboarding timelines.

We also have some compliance requirements in our RFP (attached) around SLA credits, audit log retention, and IP language. Any concise guidance or examples of how you usually recommend customers route purchases would be very helpful — we need to brief procurement by EOD Friday.

Appreciate a quick comparison and recommended default path for enterprise customers with production SLAs.

Thanks,
Katie Lin
Procurement Manager
Nimbus Analytics
Attachment: Nimbus_RFP_requirements.pdf

From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>

Cc: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-04-19T10:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Procurement routing: marketplace billing vs direct MSA — support & escalation model

Hi Katie — thanks for the clear list. Short answer up front: both routes can work for production customers, but they trade off speed of procurement vs control over SLAs, invoicing, and support handoffs. Below is a concise comparison and the recommended default for enterprise procurement.

Marketplace (AWS/Azure/GCP):
- Invoicing: Usually billed through the marketplace (vendor of record varies by cloud). Faster PO routing for some customers but invoice comes from marketplace or reseller.
- Support & escalation: Initial support is often via the marketplace portal; for deeper engineering escalations we involve Redwood but the ticket flow can be slower and lacks direct routing hooks.
- SLAs & credits: Marketplace terms are often standardized; custom SLA credits or special telemetry/audit commitments are harder to negotiate.
- Onboarding speed: Faster for smaller pilots — procurement churn is lower.

Direct MSA / Co-sell (direct invoice or reseller with co-sell):
- Invoicing: Invoice comes from Redwood (or our reseller partner depending on setup). Aligns with vendor onboarding and customer accounting practices — easier for PO-driven large-enterprise buyers.
- Support & escalation: Direct routing into Redwood support + dedicated escalation playbooks (SLA-backed response and on-call routing).
- SLAs & custom terms: We can include tailored SLA language, audit log retention, and data handling terms in the MSA or SOW.
- Onboarding speed: Slightly longer due to contracting, but avoids later friction for production workloads.

Recommendation: For Nimbus (production, compliance requirements, and explicit SLA/credit requests) I recommend pursuing a co-sell listing + direct MSA (co-sell lets you purchase through your preferred channel while the MSA preserves custom SLAs and direct support). If procurement timeline is extremely tight for a quick pilot, marketplace procurement is acceptable with the caveat that we will need a documented escalation playbook and a separate MSA negotiation before production cutover.

Next steps I can own:
- Provide a one-page escalation playbook that explains ticket routing under marketplace purchases.
- Share a pricing comparison (marketplace list vs direct negotiated) and a draft MSA (DocuSign link) — can send both by tomorrow.
- If helpful, schedule a 30-min call with our sales engineering and support ops to walk procurement/legal through ticket flows.

We have a couple of internal notes (Vanessa/Laura) on the detailed implications — tagging them for ops/legal input.

Best,
Jordan Blake
Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference

From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-04-20T09:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Procurement routing: marketplace billing vs direct MSA — support & escalation model

Jordan — quick operational notes from my side:

- Marketplace nuance: AWS Marketplace has two common models (Marketplace SaaS Contract or Reseller). In the SaaS Contract model we still act as the vendor-of-record for support but the customer opens tickets via AWS Support/Marketplace which then get routed to us — the handoff introduces a median and we lose some telemetry (ticket metadata may be limited).
- For customers requiring SLA credits, security attestations, or custom retention windows, we need a direct SOW or MSA. Marketplace terms are too rigid for non-standard credit language.
- Billing: If Nimbus wants PO-based payments tied to their AP process, a direct invoice is much simpler. Marketplace billing sometimes requires workarounds (reseller invoices, cloud provider net terms).
- Recommendation: Offer the co-sell/marketplace listing for procurement convenience, but tie production deployment to a direct MSA that includes the escalation playbook, named on-call contacts, and an agreed SLA table.

Attachments for internal reference: AWS_marketplace_support_matrix.csv

Laura — any legal red flags on offering a co-sell + post-purchase MSA approach?

From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-04-20T11:22:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Procurement routing: marketplace billing vs direct MSA — support & escalation model

Vanessa — agree with the approach. Key legal considerations: we must avoid language that implies AWS/Azure will provide technical support beyond their portal routing. Contractually, the MSA should make Redwood the party responsible for response SLAs even if procurement occurs via marketplace. We'll also need to limit warranty/liability differently for marketplace purchases if Redwood isn't the sole billing party.

I can draft a short addendum for the MSA that states: "Marketplace purchases will be covered by the terms of the MSA between Customer and Redwood; ticket escalation into Redwood support is guaranteed within the SLA table provided." That language has worked in prior co-sell deals.

Laura
General Counsel, Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Procurement routing: marketplace billing vs direct MSA — support & escalation model

Hi Katie / Evan — quick summary and recommended path based on our internal review:

1) Recommended procurement path for Nimbus: Start with a co-sell marketplace listing to keep procurement momentum, but execute a direct MSA (DocuSign link below) prior to production cutover so we can include the SLA table, audit/log retention, and named escalation contacts.

2) Support and escalation: Under the proposed approach Redwood will be contractually responsible for SLA response times and engineering escalation. In marketplace purchases the customer will open tickets through the marketplace portal but our escalation playbook will ensure direct routing into Redwood on-call and priority handling. See attached pricing comparison.

3) Invoice/PO flow: For pilot we can allow marketplace billing. For enterprise production, we recommend a direct invoice (or reseller invoice that references the MSA) to align with Nimbus AP.
